subject: Key handover operations + TLS endpoint evidence request
messages:
From: Ana Rivera <ana.rivera@helixhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@helixhealth.com, daniel.cho@helixhealth.com
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: key handover operational details + TLS evidence

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the call earlier. HelixHealth's procurement and security teams are preparing the vendor intake packet and need a concise operational playbook and evidence package for the upcoming key handover. Specifically we need the following for our internal auditors: 

- A step-by-step handover process when customer-provided keys (BYOK) are imported or when keys are escrowed with an HSM vendor (physical transfer, manifests, attestation).
- Tamper-evident packaging and courier procedures for hardware HSM seed exports (if applicable).
- The exact TLS termination model for hosted endpoints (where certs live, whether there is TLS termination at load balancer or at instance, and mTLS support).
- Evidence of TLS cert chains and OCSP/CRL endpoints used by your production gateways.
- Audit log locations and retention for key import/export events (S3 path or internal log ids acceptable).

Can you provide a single playbook PDF and a manifest template we can use? We also need a contact and a 2-hour window to schedule a recorded handover/demo with your ops team.

We'd like this by EOD Monday (Aug 2) if possible.

Thanks,
Ana Rivera
Vendor Security, HelixHealth

Subject: Re: Request: key handover operational details + TLS evidence

Hi Ana —

Appreciate the clear ask. I pulled together an operational playbook and a manifest template that cover both BYOK import flows and physical HSM seed transfers. Attached: key-handover-playbook.pdf (detailed checklist + roles/responsibilities) and handover-manifest.csv (CSV template).

Quick summary here so your auditors can triage:

- BYOK import (software key wrap):
  - Customer uploads wrapped key via secure upload endpoint (signed URL + mutual TLS)
  - Import job runs in isolated staging tenant; KMS only accepts keys wrapped with customer-provided wrapping key material
  - Import events emit audit records to: s3://redwood-audit/helix/keys/imports/ (retention 7 years) and to our SIEM (retention policy per contract)

- HSM seed export (physical):
  - We coordinate with vendor-approved couriers (listed in playbook)
  - Seed export requires 2-person ops witness, tamper-evident container, manifest signed by both witnesses, and chain-of-custody scanned and uploaded to secure Drive link (see related_links)
  - Customer-facing attestation: we provide signed export attestation (PKCS#7) and redacted photos of tamper seals on request

- TLS endpoints and termination:
  - Production ingress TLS is terminated at our edge gateway (Redwood Edge) backed by hardware acceleration; TLS certs are stored in our KMS and rotated automatically.
  - For dedicated/private deployments we support TLS termination at customer-hosted LB or at instance level per customer requirement.
  - mTLS is supported for customer admin APIs and for the BYOK upload endpoint (mutual certs required).
  - Certificate OCSP responder: ocsp.redwood.ai (primary), ocsp-secondary.redwood.ai (failover). CRLs are maintained for longer-lived certs and available on request.

I've looped in Marcus (ops) and Priya (crypto/engineering) for technical follow-up and to propose a 2-hour window. Marcus — can you propose your earliest availability on Mon/Tue? Priya — can you attach the TLS cert bundles and the short evidence archive?

Attachments: key-handover-playbook.pdf; handover-manifest.csv

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Technical Partnerships

Laura —

Thanks for the speedy reply and the playbook. A few follow-ups from our security engineering team: 

1) For the BYOK import flow, can you confirm whether Redwood ever retains an unwrapped customer key in memory or on disk at any point during the import? We need explicit statement for our risk register.
2) For HSM seed exports, can you name the approved courier partners and confirm whether chain-of-custody documents are timestamped with NTP-validated time sources?
3) For TLS certs: can you provide the full cert chain used by production edge (PEM bundle) and OCSP responder AIA URLs for each cert? We also need the last rotation date for the edge cert.

We can take the attachments offline if required. The security team would also like a 2-hour window beginning Aug 4 13:00-15:00 PDT for a live handover/demonstration (recorded).

Regards,
Daniel Cho
Procurement, HelixHealth

Subject: Re: Request: key handover operational details + TLS evidence

Hi Daniel / Ana —

PR answers and attachments attached (tls-endpoint-certs.zip includes PEM chain, intermediates, and OCSP AIA URIs). Summary below for auditors: 

1) BYOK import memory/disk handling:
   - At no point do we persist an unencrypted (unwrapped) customer key to disk. Import flow uses an in-memory unwrap within a short-lived, isolated import sandbox (Linux kernel namespaces + tmpfs) and the unwrapped key material is immediately wrapped into our HSM-backed KMS key slot.
   - We record the import event with a unique import_id; audit record contains import_id, wrap-alg, import-source IP, UTC timestamp, operator id if human-cleared. Audit records are pushed to s3://redwood-audit/helix/keys/imports/IMPORT_ID.json and an identical record is emitted to our SIEM via Syslog over TLS.

2) Approved couriers & chain-of-custody timestamping:
   - Approved couriers for HSM seed exports: SecureHaul Logistics (tracking: SHL-), IronCourier (IC-), and VaultLine (VL-). These are listed in the playbook.
   - Chain-of-custody manifests include NTP-synchronized timestamps generated by our ops witness devices (stratum-1 NTP pool, logs include NTP server IP and RTT). Photos of sealed containers include EXIF timestamp and GPS bounding box if permitted by customer.

3) TLS certs / OCSP / rotation: 
   - PEM bundle attached (tls-endpoint-certs.zip) contains: root.pem, intermediate.pem, edge-cert.pem. AIA/OCSP URIs are included in the certificate metadata files inside the zip (ocsp.redwood.ai, ocsp-secondary.redwood.ai).
   - Edge certificate last rotated: 2027-06-28T02:12:00Z (automated rotation job id: rot-20270628-42). Rotation events are logged to s3://redwood-certs/rotations/rot-20270628-42.json.

Additional operational notes:
- Export attestation: we provide a PKCS#7-signed attestation for physical exports. Attestations are signed with our export-attest key (key id attest-01) and include the manifest hash.
- Role separation: all export jobs require two distinct ops approvals (2-person control) and are gated by a time-limited approval token issued by our tickets system.
- Scheduling: Marcus will own the demo window operations and will be present for the recorded handover. Marcus — confirmed availability Aug 4, 13:00-15:00 PDT works for our ops team.

Attachments included in this message:
- tls-endpoint-certs.zip (PEM chain + cert metadata)
- handover-manifest.csv (filled example row for HelixHealth)
- key-handover-playbook.pdf (finalized; includes courier SLAs and witness checklist)

If you need signed attestations or additional SIEM excerpts (redacted), we can prepare those before the demo.

Thanks,
